title: The relation between global palm distribution and climate
problem: The use of fossil palms in palaeoclimate reconstructions is problematic due to a wide and poorly constrained minimum temperature tolerance threshold (2–8°C CMMT), which is further confounded by the widespread cultivation of palms outside their natural ranges, leading to large interpretive discrepancies and challenging climate models.
method: We propose a method that uses a manually filtered dataset of over 20,000 georeferenced palm records, combined with probability density analysis, to derive statistically robust climatic thresholds for various palm taxonomic ranks to refine their use as palaeoclimate proxies.
task: The task is to determine quantitative temperature thresholds for the global distribution of palms by statistically analyzing a large, filtered dataset of georeferenced occurrences to refine their use as palaeoclimatic proxies for interpreting the fossil record.
innovation: By analyzing a manually filtered dataset of over 20,000 palm records, this paper statistically defines new, taxonomically-specific climate thresholds for the Arecaceae family, establishing a robust Cold Month Mean Temperature of >5.2°C, which refines the use of palms as a palaeoclimatic proxy.
